body:
We tested this head in an offline VM running a copy of the actual AGIECUT Classic Cut 2S control. An independent Rust caller used befdc57f9 to emit the full CCSEP20.SBL and CCSEP20.SBR files. We loaded these files with the caller-prepared synthetic CCSEP20.ISO. Their SHA-256 values were:

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| CCSEP20.SBL | aadf92ae8dfe705cef39800c7e5a0d5cd31b97231b3ffb8221b477537ead5d97 |
| CCSEP20.SBR | 0d400ea1340f288eaebba4001881f45aaae1e65a8e4d4af817bfaf5833ee3857 |
| CCSEP20.ISO | 2d258373529825d552536bf1ec5e830f0194c6633583fb782c911949d6853fd6 |

The newly created piece showed CUT1, CCB030[0] and CCSEP20.ISO:1. The work had zero erosion steps. The control showed a closed counterclockwise punch, 1.0 mm separation and 20 mm stock height. The start hole was 2.0 mm in diameter at X−30.000, Y0.000. The wire was Berco Cut 0.25 mm.

FORMALCHECK blocked the work because the technology was undefined. We did not assign technology or generate working steps. No physical cut was performed.

<!-- pr-reviewer: befdc57f9e4dea4c4efd4f623d16dc45562115fb -->
**Review: clean (read, not built).** Head befdc57f9. Label: merge-ready. P1 set from the linked issue #2984. Outside contributor: the maintainer approves and merges by hand.

What the change does:
- New public module `camcraft_post::agie_setup`: `PunchSetup20::encode` writes a JEScript piece (SBL) and an import manifest (SBR) for one closed punch on 20 mm steel 0001 with Berco 0.25 wire, Ra 0.30 and 1 mm separation, with zero erosion steps on import. No existing post output changes; no UI or workspace writer calls this yet.
- Validation comes before any bytes: DOS stem rule with the device-name list, increasing stock bounds inside the 350 x 250 mm span, and the whole 2 mm start hole inside the stock. Coordinates are integer micrometres; the `mm` formatter splits through i64, so no float rounding enters a record.
- Every `JE_Create*`/`JE_AttribObject` that matters is wrapped in the checked() guard: a failed attribute stops the script on the control instead of leaving a half-built piece.

Checks I made:
- The encoder is a literal emitter; I read all 273 lines. The technology fields (CCB030, "0.30,1.50,1.00,F,F,F"), the COMMPOINT and SEPCUT values, and the start-point path match the review text and the golden bytes.
- `device_names_paths_and_script_text_cannot_enter_an_agie_record` is the right defensive law to pin, and the table `stock_and_full_start_hole_must_fit_the_setup_span` covers the hole radius edge.
- `.gitattributes` marks `golden/agie-setup/*` with `-text`, so the tested CRLF bytes survive checkout on every platform. `mm()` keeps the sign split exact for negative coordinates.
- Clean-room: the Agie reference is the contributor's own MIT implementation, named with its notice in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`. No HSMWorks material is involved. The two golden files are stated as synthetic examples.
- Second commit befdc57f9 only sharpens the import instructions and the review text; no behaviour change in the encoder beyond the string.

Not built here: pr-test.yml cannot run a contributor's code. The author's report on this head: quick gate 107 steps green, reached heavy gate 197 steps green, clippy clean, one independent caller reproduced both files byte for byte. Those are the author's runs; they are recorded, not verified here.

Note: this is a new machine-file format under the safety floor. A read-only second review at the safety tier precedes the merge, and the merge itself is the maintainer's.
